assessment.nobel_worthiness: A fundamental account of how firm heterogeneity and selection shape trade patterns and welfare, with unusually broad influence across trade and applied microeconomics.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is central to the canonical heterogeneous-firm framework; Redding made major related theoretical and quantitative contributions. Credit boundaries with other trade theorists remain important.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been extensively developed, tested and used for more than two decades.
uncertainties: The appropriate balance between the canonical model and its intellectual precursors is contestable.
The discovery spans a broad literature rather than one isolated result.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural empirical industrial organization transformed measurement of demand, competition and policy counterfactuals in imperfectly competitive markets.
assessment.attribution: Pakes, Berry and Levinsohn are directly associated with foundational approaches to estimating differentiated-product demand and dynamic industry models, though the listed contribution has many indispensable contributors.
assessment.maturity: The methods are deeply embedded in applied IO and have generated a large body of empirical work.
uncertainties: Attribution is unusually diffuse among the seven credited names.
Structural conclusions can depend strongly on modeling assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their analysis gave political economy a durable, rigorous framework for explaining trade policy and protection.
assessment.attribution: Helpman and Grossman are the clearly identifiable partnership behind the core political-economy models of protection.
assessment.maturity: The work is longstanding and remains a central reference point in international-trade research.
uncertainties: The empirical fit of stylized special-interest models varies across institutions and settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This research made management practices and organizational capital measurable economic objects and linked them convincingly to productivity.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen originated much of the measurement agenda, while Sadun made major contributions to its extension and organizational implications.
assessment.maturity: A substantial international empirical literature has accumulated, with findings influential in firm and productivity research.
uncertainties: Separating causal management effects from selection and complementary inputs remains difficult.
Survey-based measures invite concerns about comparability.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative Ricardian trade models supplied a powerful framework for measuring the welfare consequences of trade and trade costs.
assessment.attribution: Kortum, Costinot and Rodriguez-Clare are prominent contributors to the modern quantitative Ricardian program, though its roots and later extensions are broad.
assessment.maturity: The approach is well established and widely used in quantitative policy analysis.
uncertainties: Welfare estimates rely on restrictive model structure and trade-elasticity measurement.
Attribution overlaps with earlier Ricardian and gravity-based work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work provided foundational economic analysis of information goods, network effects and competition in digital markets.
assessment.attribution: Shapiro, Varian and Katz are strongly associated with the core economic framework, although related contributions by Farrell and later scholars are substantial.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have had lasting scholarly and policy relevance and became more consequential with digital-market growth.
uncertainties: The umbrella contribution covers several distinct literatures.
Fast-changing platforms complicate assessment of the most durable elements.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Misallocation research sharpened quantitative explanations of cross-country productivity and income differences by focusing attention on factor allocation across firms.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow are central to the influential empirical framework; Restuccia made major connected contributions to its development and interpretation.
assessment.maturity: The framework has generated extensive theoretical, measurement and policy-oriented follow-up research.
uncertainties: Measured wedges may combine distortions with adjustment costs, demand shocks and specification error.
Estimated aggregate gains can be sensitive to assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theoretical and empirical analysis of adverse selection substantially advanced understanding of insurance markets and their policy design.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav and Salanie are leading contributors to the modern measurement and modeling of selection, while the foundational theory has a wider lineage.
assessment.maturity: The work has been tested in numerous insurance settings and is highly influential in applied microeconomics.
uncertainties: The size and direction of selection differ materially across markets.
Attribution must distinguish this modern empirical program from earlier foundational insurance theory.
